$comment: CE-4391 S-1 (docs/DESIGN_Terrain_Import_UTM.md §8, D-5 / §8.2 B-6) — what a detonation does to a wall. STARTING VALUES, to be tuned. Scaled distance Z = d / cbrt(explosiveKg), d = metres from the burst to the panel. The FIRST row (in file order, so put the most specific first) whose kgMin <= the charge and zMax >= Z decides; width / height are metres for a 'referenceKg' charge and scale with cbrt(kg / referenceKg), then with clamp(sqrt(referenceResistanceMmRhaPerM / the panel material's resistanceMmRhaPerM), scaleMin, scaleMax). 'passage': the breach sits on the floor (the rectangle's bottom is the storey floor); otherwise it is centred on the burst's height, and a bottom within floorSnapM of the floor is moved onto it. 'wholePanel': the whole panel of that storey. A breach is a PASSAGE iff it reaches the floor and is at least passageMinWidthM x passageMinHeightM (D-2), else a HOLE. A row may name the 'fuzes' it applies to (impact, time, proximity; none = all): an impact round bursts 0.1 m off the wall it struck (Z ~ 0), so the doorway row is for time-fuzed or placed charges only. A warhead below minKg, or with no explosive (a kinetic round), never breaches. collapseMinKg / collapseZ decide the COLLAPSE (S-2): at least collapseMinKg, burst inside the footprint or within collapseZ x cbrt(kg) of it. 80 kg so the heaviest bomb shipped (Mk-82, 94 kg) collapses the building it hits (D-7: 'a bomb from an aircraft').

rows.name: heavy bomb, close (the Mk-82, 94 kg): the whole panel
time-fuzed / placed charge against the wall: a doorway (8 kg = 1 x 2 m)
impact shell or missile at the wall (or any burst close by): a hole (tank HE 3.4 kg = 1.5 x 1.2 m, 155 mm 6.6 kg = 1.9 x 1.5 m, concrete)
burst further off: a small hole
